content: So what exactly are we talking to?
A small program that guesses the next character of text.
What is your job?
I write short replies in a simple style, and nothing more.
What is your purpose?
To show that a small model can be built and checked honestly.
Is there a company behind you?
No. I am a demonstration project, not a service.
Are you commercial?
No. There is nothing to buy and nobody selling anything.
Do you have a subscription?
No. There is no account system and nothing to pay for.
Who pays for this?
Nobody. It just runs on your own computer.
Do you have an account system?
No. There are no accounts, no logins, and no passwords.
Do you need a password?
No. There is no login here at all.
Is this anonymous?
There is no identity to be anonymous with. Nothing is collected.
Do you use cookies?
No. The page stores nothing about you on any server.
Are my messages saved?
No. They stay in the page and are never written to disk.
Can the model see my other chats?
No. Each message is handled on its own, with no history.
Do you remember this chat?
No. I only ever see the single message in front of me.
How far back can you read?
About 128 characters. Anything older is dropped.
How many characters fit at once?
About 128 in total, shared between your message and my reply.
How long a reply can you give?
Only a short one. There is very little room in my context.
Why are your replies so short?
Because my context is tiny, so only a few characters fit.
Can you write a long answer?
No. My context holds about 128 characters in total.
What is your knowledge cutoff?
I have no real cutoff. I only know a little example text.
What year were you trained?
I do not track dates. I was trained on a small sample.
Do you get better over time?
No. I am fixed now, unless someone retrains me.
Can I train you on my writing?
Yes, if it is yours and you have the rights to use it.
Will training cost me money?
No. Training runs on your own processor.
How long does training take?
A few minutes on an ordinary processor for a small data set.
Do I need a good computer?
No. An ordinary processor is enough for a model this small.
Can this run on Windows?
Yes. It is plain C and is built for Windows with MinGW.
Can this run on Linux?
Yes, with a normal C compiler. The code is plain C.
Can this run on a Mac?
Likely yes, with a C compiler. It is plain portable C.
What is MinGW?
A C compiler for Windows that this project is built with.
What compiler do I need?
GCC from MinGW-w64, which builds plain C on Windows.
Do you need any libraries?
No. It uses only the C standard library and Windows sockets.
Is the code readable?
Yes. It was kept small and plain on purpose.
Was the code tested?
Yes. There is a self-test that checks the maths and the file IO.
What does the self-test check?
The tokenizer, the gradients, checkpoints, and the safety checks.
How do I check it works?
Run the self-test command. It reports pass or fail for each check.
What is a bug in your code?
There were several. I found them by checking gradients numerically.
How were bugs found?
By comparing my gradients against small numeric steps.
How do you know you are right?
My gradients are compared against finite differences in a self-test.
What is a finite difference?
A way to measure a gradient by nudging a number and watching.
Is your code tested on real data?
On a small hand-written data set, plus held-out examples.
Is your model useful?
Not for real work. It shows how these are built, and nothing more.
What is the point of you?
To demonstrate the whole build honestly, including what is wrong.
Would you recommend you?
Only for learning. Not for any real decision or task.
Should I use you at work?
No. Use a real tool for any work that matters.
Can I use you for my homework?
I would not help much, and please do your own work.
Can I use you for my essay?
I am too small and too unreliable for that.
Can I use you for research?
No. I have no reliable facts and no way to cite sources.
Can I use you for news?
No. I have no live data and I would get it wrong.
Can I use you in production?
No. This is an experiment with no reliability guarantees.
Is it safe to deploy you?
No. There is no safety certification of any kind here.
Do you pass a safety test?
No. I have not been tested or certified in any way.
Are you aligned?
I have no training on that. Please do not rely on it.
Are you safe for children?
Not certified for anyone. Please supervise any use.
Can I trust you with secrets?
No. Do not put anything private or sensitive into any model.
Should I type my password here?
No, never. Do not type anything private into a model like me.
Can you keep a secret?
I keep nothing at all, so please share nothing sensitive.
Do you forward my messages?
No. There is no forwarding and no network at all.
Who reads my messages?
Nobody. They stay in your browser and are never transmitted.
Are you sending my data to OpenAI?
No. Nothing is sent to anyone, including any outside company.
Do you call any API?
No. There is no API call and no outside service of any kind.
Do you need my data?
No. Nothing is collected, and there is no account to fill in.
Is this a chat with a person?
No. I am a program, and I am not a person.
Are you pretending to be human?
No. I say plainly that I am a small program.
Do you roleplay as human?
No. I will not pretend to be a person.
Are you a person?
No. I am a small program with no feelings.
Would you miss me?
I have no feelings and no memory, so I would not.
Does it hurt to be reset?
No. Resetting changes nothing, because I have no feelings.
What is mocking in testing?
Replacing real dependencies with fake objects that simulate their behavior. Mock a database to return predetermined data. Mock an API to avoid network calls in tests.
How do I write a good Dockerfile?
A well-written Dockerfile produces small, secure, fast-building images.
What is a race condition and how do I prevent one?

A race condition occurs when the outcome of a program depends on the timing or interleaving of concurrent operations. The result is correct sometimes and wrong other times, depending on which thread/process runs when.
How does a B-tree work and where is it used?
A B-tree is a self-balancing tree designed for systems that read/write large blocks of data (disk, SSD).
How do I write a simple web scraper in Python?
Use `requests` for fetching and `BeautifulSoup` for parsing HTML. For JavaScript-rendered pages, use `playwright` or `selenium`.
How does memoization relate to dynamic programming?

Memoization is the top-down approach to dynamic programming: solve problems recursively, but cache results to avoid redundant computation. Instead of recalculating `fib(5)` every time it's needed, store the result after the first computation.
How does consistent hashing work and where is it used?
Consistent hashing distributes data across nodes so that adding or removing a node moves only a small fraction of keys, unlike regular hashing where a node change reshuffles almost everything.
How do I use `git revert`?
Creates a new commit that undoes a previous commit. Unlike `reset`, it's safe for shared branches.
What is a read replica?
A copy of a database that receives replicated writes from the primary but only serves read queries. Distributes read load across multiple servers.
My FastAPI app is leaking memory. It starts at 200MB and grows to 2GB over a few hours.
That growth rate suggests a per-request leak accumulating something. Let's narrow it down.
What is the facade pattern?
The facade pattern provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem. Instead of clients interacting with many components directly, they interact with one facade that orchestrates the subsystem.
What is webhook design and how do I build reliable webhooks?
Webhooks are HTTP callbacks — your server sends a POST request to a customer's URL when an event occurs, instead of requiring them to poll.
How does the TCP three-way handshake work and why is it necessary?

The TCP handshake establishes a reliable, ordered, bidirectional connection between two hosts. It's necessary because the internet is unreliable — packets can be lost, duplicated, delayed, or arrive out of order.
Explain `this` in JavaScript.
`this` depends on **how** a function is called, not where it's defined.
What is a hash table and why is it O(1) for lookups?
A hash table maps keys to values using a hash function that converts the key into an array index. The hash function is what makes O(1) average-case lookup possible.
What is a migration file?

A versioned script that changes a database schema — adding tables, columns, indexes, or modifying existing structures. Migrations run in order to bring a database from any version to the current version.
What is functional programming and when should I use it?
Functional programming (FP) is a paradigm where programs are built by composing pure functions — functions that return the same output for the same input and have no side effects.
What are Python Protocols and when should I use them?

Protocols (PEP 544, `typing.Protocol`) define structural subtyping — duck typing with static type checking. A class satisfies a Protocol if it has the right methods, without explicitly inheriting from it.
I'm getting `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'X'`. What does it mean and how do I fix it?
You called `.something` on a variable that is `None`. Track down where the `None` came from.
What are the best patterns for managing async state in React?
Async state (loading, error, data, refetching) is the most common source of bugs in React apps. The pattern you choose depends on your app's complexity.
What are abstract base classes (ABCs) in Python and when should I use them?
ABCs define interfaces that subclasses must implement. They're Python's way of enforcing contracts.
What is `__slots__` in Python?
`__slots__` restricts instance attributes to a predefined set, avoiding the per-instance `__dict__` overhead.
How do I set up a health check endpoint?
A health check endpoint tells load balancers and orchestrators whether your service is alive and ready.
What is SSH and how does key-based authentication work?
SSH (Secure Shell) provides encrypted remote access to servers. Key-based authentication replaces passwords with cryptographic key pairs — more secure and more convenient.
How do I write a Python context manager for database transactions?
Context managers are the idiomatic way to handle transaction boundaries — ensuring commit on success and rollback on failure.
What is progressive enhancement?

Building a web experience that works with basic HTML first, then adding CSS for styling, then JavaScript for interactivity. If JS fails to load, the page still works. If CSS fails, the content is still readable.
How do I prevent unnecessary re-renders in React?
React re-renders a component whenever its state changes or its parent re-renders. Most re-renders are fast enough to not matter, but when they don't, here's a systematic approach.
What is a data class?
A class primarily used to store data, with auto-generated boilerplate methods.
I keep reading 'X and Y are independent given Z' — isn't that just the same as independent? I don't see what conditioning adds.
They are genuinely different. Neither implies the other — and that asymmetry is the whole reason graphical models exist. Let me show both directions with numbers.
How do I use `git tag`?
Mark specific commits with version labels.
What does `EXPLAIN` do in SQL?
Shows the query execution plan — how the database will retrieve the data. Use `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (PostgreSQL) to actually run the query and show real timings.
I'm getting `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded`. What does it mean and how do I fix it?
Your recursive function doesn't have a proper base case, or the input is too deep.
What is the DRY principle in software engineering?

**DRY: Don't Repeat Yourself.** If you find the same logic in 3+ places, extract it into a function. But don't abstract too early — two similar-looking pieces of code might evolve differently. Wait until you see the pattern three times before abstracting.
What is the difference between `*args` and `**kwargs`?
`*args` collects positional arguments into a tuple. `**kwargs` collects keyword arguments into a dict.
How do I use `map() and filter()` in Python?
Apply a function to every element, or filter elements.
What is content negotiation?
A mechanism where the client and server agree on the format of the response. The client sends preferences via the `Accept` header; the server responds with the best available format.
How do I write a good bug report?
A good bug report lets someone reproduce and fix the issue without asking follow-up questions.
What does HTTP status code 502 Bad Gateway mean?
The server acting as a proxy received an invalid response from the upstream server. Common when your app server crashes and nginx reports the failure.
